profile: Marketing assistant, 29, English, installs a firewall for the first time after reading that apps phone home. Reads onboarding text, but has no idea what a VPN or DNS is.
goal: Turn the firewall on, block the internet for one app on Wi-Fi and on mobile data, and understand what the app did.

profile: Accountant, 52, Slovak, phone set to Slovak. Reads English only a little. Careful, reads every dialog before tapping.
goal: Understand what the app is for and block one app's mobile data. Note every screen that is not in Slovak or mixes languages.

profile: Engineer, 45, German, privacy-minded, notices awkward or cut-off German labels (long compound words).
goal: Set up the firewall, turn on DNS blocking with a preset list, and check that the logs show what was blocked.

profile: Pharmacist, 39, reads Arabic, expects every screen to flow right to left.
goal: Do the main task end to end (firewall on, block one app on Wi-Fi) and check that text, icons, toggles and arrows are mirrored.

profile: Retired nurse, 74, low vision, uses Android's largest font size (200%) and high contrast text.
goal: Read every screen and block one app without zooming. Report any text or toggle that is cut, overlaps or cannot be reached.

profile: Student, 17, English, old small phone with a low-resolution screen, taps fast.
goal: Get through setup and block one app on mobile data. Report anything that does not fit this small screen.

profile: Teacher, 47, uses the family tablet, reads Spanish, wants to keep the kids' games off the internet.
goal: Use the app on the big screen: block a few apps, try the search and the app details screen, and judge whether the layout uses the space.

profile: Student, 21, English, dark mode everywhere, skips every text, taps fast, changes the app's colors and styles.
goal: Reach the firewall as fast as possible, then try the Colors & Styles settings and check dark mode contrast on every screen.

profile: Accessibility consultant, 41, English, red-green color blind, uses a screen reader on and off. Judges whether every control has a spoken name and whether allowed/blocked state is shown by more than color.
goal: Block and unblock one app on Wi-Fi and mobile data and check that the state of each toggle can be told without color and that every icon button has a name in the accessibility tree.

profile: Sysadmin, 35, English, power user who has used NetGuard and AFWall+. Tests edge cases and checks that rules really apply.
goal: Test the firewall rules: block an app on Wi-Fi only, then mobile data only, switch networks and verify each rule, try block-by-default settings, system apps, search, logs and DNS blocking.
